claim:
For every \(\lambda>1\), let \(X_\lambda=(\mathbb R^2,N_\lambda)\) with
\[
N_\lambda(x_1,x_2)=\max\left\{\lambda|x_1|,\sqrt{x_1^2+x_2^2}\right\}.
\]
Then
\[
d_{\mathrm{BM}}(X_\lambda,\ell_2^2)^2=C_{\mathrm{NJ}}(X_\lambda)=2-\lambda^{-2}.
\]
An optimal Euclidean pullback norm is, up to positive scaling,
\[
|(x_1,x_2)|_*=\sqrt{x_1^2+\lambda^{-2}x_2^2}.
\]
integrity: The Banach--Mazur optimization starts from an arbitrary positive-definite quadratic pullback; coordinate-sign averaging is proved not to worsen the two-sided comparison, and the remaining one-variable minimization is exact. The von Neumann--Jordan equality is independently witnessed by an explicit vector pair and the Euclidean parallelogram bound; no finite experiment is used as proof.
scientific_limitations: Restricted to the real two-dimensional Banaś--Frączek family with lambda greater than one. The proof supplies an optimal Euclidean pullback but does not classify all optimal isomorphisms. The 2014 same-object source was inspected through abstract and bibliographic records rather than full text, leaving a residual bibliographic risk of an unindexed or passing prior exact-distance statement.
title: Exact Euclidean Banach--Mazur distance of the Banaś--Frączek plane
